text:
A keloid is a raised, firm scar that grows beyond the edges of the original wound because of excessive collagen production. Neither option in the team note fits: it isn't a fine, hairline scar, and it isn't something that forms when a wound drain is removed too soon. If I must choose, "a fine, hairline scar" is the less wrong of the two, since it is at least a type of scar, but it is the opposite of a keloid.

CONFIDENCE: 90
